🧪 Learning

Test set

In simple words

Examples put aside before training and used only to check how well a model does on data it has never seen.

Part of the examples that is kept away from the model during training. Because the model never learned from them, its score on the test set is a fair estimate of how it will do on new, real examples. Testing on the training data instead can hide overfitting.

Example. From 1,000 labelled photos, you train on 800 and keep 200 as the test set. The score on those 200 is the one you report.

Related words

  • OverfittingWhen a model memorises its training examples so closely that it does badly on new data.
  • GeneralisationA model's ability to work well on new examples it has never seen, not just on its training data.
  • DatasetA large, organised collection of examples used to train or test an AI model.
  • Decision treeA model that answers by asking a chain of yes/no questions about an example, like a flowchart.
  • AccuracyThe share of examples a model gets right, usually measured on a test set.
